statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumours with high WTAP levels had worse prognosis in adrenocortical carcinoma, lower-grade glioma, hepatocellular carcinoma and ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma.
statements.evidence: High WTAP expression was significantly associated with poor prognosis in adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), brain lower-grade glioma (LGG), liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC), and ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma (OV).
statements.note: The results name these four tumour types as the ones where high WTAP expression went with poor prognosis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Melanoma and thymoma run the other way: patients with low WTAP expression survived longer in those two tumour types.
statements.evidence: In contrast, low WTAP expression correlated with improved survival in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) and thymoma (THYM).
statements.note: The abstract reports the opposite prognostic direction for SKCM and THYM, where low expression tracked with improved survival.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Knocking down WTAP in tumour cell lines slowed their proliferation.
statements.evidence: GSEA indicated that WTAP predominantly contributes to cell cycle regulation, thereby promoting tumorigenesis.
statements.note: The cell-cycle link comes from pathway enrichment analysis of expression data; no knockdown or proliferation experiment is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: WTAP expression rose together with infiltration of B cells, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, macrophages and neutrophils.
statements.evidence: WTAP expression demonstrated a positive correlation with immune cell infiltration, including B cells, CD4 + T cells, CD8 + T cells, dendritic cells, macrophages, and neutrophils.
statements.note: A positive correlation with infiltration of exactly these immune cell populations is among the reported results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A number of 5mC regulatory factors were expressed abnormally in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and that abnormality was significantly linked to somatic mutations.
statements.evidence: (1) Several 5mC regulatory factors were found to be abnormally expressed in HNSCC, with a significant association with somatic mutations.
statements.note: The first reported result is abnormal expression of several 5mC regulatory factors together with a significant association with somatic mutations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Expression of 5mC regulatory genes in HNSCC differs between anatomical subsites such as oral cavity and larynx.
statements.evidence: Using expression profile data from the GEO and TCGA databases, the study analyzed the differential expression of 5mC-related genes, their connection with somatic mutations, and their impact on the immune microenvironment.
statements.note: Differential expression is reported for HNSCC as a whole, with no breakdown of the cohort by tumour subsite.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumours differing in 5mC methylation regulation pattern also differed in immune infiltration, immune checkpoint expression, tumour mutation burden and cancer stem cell gene set expression.
statements.evidence: (2) Different 5mC methylation regulation patterns showed variations in immune infiltration, immune checkpoint expression, tumor mutation burden, and cancer stem cell gene set expression, potentially influencing immunotherapy effectiveness and prognosis.
statements.note: These four features are listed as varying across the different 5mC regulation patterns.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DNMT1 and TET2 were among the prognosis-related risk genes that predicted survival outcomes in HNSCC patients.
statements.evidence: (3) Prognosis-related risk genes, such as DNMT1 and TET2, were identified as predictors of survival outcomes in HNSCC patients.
statements.note: Both genes are named as identified predictors of survival in the reported results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: cfDNA taken from the mutant cells' culture medium had size distributions resembling the hypofragmented profiles reported earlier in plasma of p.R206C carriers.
statements.evidence: We analyzed the cfDNA composition directly from conditioned culture medium and found that fragment size distributions in mutant cells mimics the hypofragmented profiles previously observed in plasma samples from p.R206C carriers.
statements.note: That the mutant cells' cfDNA reproduces the carriers' hypofragmented size profile is the central reported finding.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pre-treating plasma from p.R206C carriers with DNASE1L3 improved detection of tumour variants in a cancer cohort.
statements.evidence: This could open avenues for DNASE1L3 as a candidate pre-treatment agent to improve the accuracy and efficiency of cfDNA sequencing-based diagnostics in hypofragmented liquid biopsies.
statements.note: Pre-treatment is raised only as a prospect the in vitro result opens up; no patient samples or diagnostic performance are tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Treating hypofragmented cfDNA in vitro with recombinant wild-type DNASE1L3 enriched mononucleosomal fragments and left end-motifs characteristic of DNASE1L3 cleavage.
statements.evidence: We also showed that in vitro treatment of hypofragmented cfDNA with recombinant wildtype DNASE1L3 could enrich for mononucleosomal fragments, with fragment end-motifs characteristic of DNASE1L3 cleavage activity.
statements.note: Both the enrichment of mononucleosomal fragments and the characteristic end-motifs are reported for the in vitro treatment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The model is an isogenic HEK293T line made by CRISPR prime editing, so that R206C DNASE1L3 is expressed from the endogenous locus rather than a plasmid.
statements.evidence: we developed an isogenic HEK293T cell line model by using CRISPR Prime Editing for endogenous expression of DNASE1L3 R206C
statements.note: The abstract states the model was built by prime editing for endogenous expression, in contrast to the plasmid overexpression of earlier work.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A Tn6022-like transposon targets the comM gene through TnsF, a protein whose tyrosine recombinase domain is inactivated.
statements.evidence: We experimentally characterized a CAST I-D system and a Tn6022-like transposon that uses TnsF, which contains an inactivated tyrosine recombinase domain, to target the comM gene.
statements.note: The experimentally characterised Tn6022-like transposon is described as using an inactivated-recombinase TnsF to target comM.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tsy, a transposon outside the Tn7 family, encodes a TnsF homolog with an intact tyrosine recombinase domain and also inserts into comM.
statements.evidence: Additionally, we identified a non-Tn7 transposon, Tsy, encoding a homolog of TnsF with an active tyrosine recombinase domain, which we show also inserts into comM.
statements.note: Tsy is reported as a non-Tn7 element whose TnsF homolog retains an active domain and which inserts into the same gene.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: RNA-guided targeting in CRISPR-associated transposons is more specific than the protein-guided targeting used by other Tn7 elements.
statements.evidence: Tn7-like transposons employ multiple mechanisms for target-site selection, including protein-guided targeting and, in CRISPR-associated transposons (CASTs), RNA-guided targeting.
statements.note: Both targeting modes are named, but no comparison of their specificity is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The phylogenomic and structural survey of target selectors turned up target-selector proteins not previously characterised, carried by newly discovered transposable elements.
statements.evidence: Combining phylogenomic and structural analyses, we conducted a broad survey of target selectors, revealing diverse mechanisms used by Tn7 to recognize target sites, including previously uncharacterized target-selector proteins found in newly discovered transposable elements (TEs).
statements.note: The survey is reported as revealing previously uncharacterised target selectors in newly discovered elements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: AK-specific keratinocytes form a discrete population in the dysplastic basal epidermis carrying the SBS7b UV signature, high mutational burden, and recurrent 9p loss and 8q gain.
statements.evidence: We identify AK-specific keratinocytes (ASK), a discrete population localized to the dysplastic basal epidermis and characterized by UV-associated mutational signatures (SBS7b), high mutational burden, and recurrent copy number alterations including 9p loss and 8q gain.
statements.note: The location, mutational signature, burden and the two recurrent copy number changes are all reported for the ASK population.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Actinic keratosis lesions containing more AK-specific keratinocytes progress to invasive cSCC more often than lesions with fewer.
statements.evidence: These findings define the molecular identity of a pre-invasive malignant keratinocyte population governed by p63/PITX1 and distinguish early oncogenic programs shared with invasive cSCC from later-acquired invasion effectors
statements.note: AK is profiled once per biopsy and compared with published cSCC data; no lesion is followed over time for progression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IGFBP6 acted as a pro-proliferative factor in keratinocytes derived from actinic keratosis.
statements.evidence: Functional experiments identify IGFBP6 as a pro-proliferative factor in AK-derived keratinocytes.
statements.note: The functional experiments are reported as showing IGFBP6 drives proliferation in AK-derived keratinocytes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ASK share tumour-propagating networks including IGFBP6, IGFBP2 and ITGA6 with cSCC tumour-specific keratinocytes, but lack the invasion effectors MMP1, MMP10 and PTHLH.
statements.evidence: Comparison with published cSCC data reveals that ASK share core tumor-propagating gene networks with tumor-specific keratinocytes (TSK), including IGFBP6, IGFBP2, and ITGA6, but lack invasion effectors MMP1, MMP10, and PTHLH.
statements.note: The comparison with published cSCC data reports exactly this shared set and this missing set of genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Bacterial diversity inside tumour tissue was lower, while anaerobes and periodontopathogens such as Dialister pneumosintes and Prevotella intermedia were more prevalent there.
statements.evidence: The diversity of the bacteria was less within tumor tissues and anaerobic bacteria and periodontopathogens (e.g., Dialister pneumosintes and Prevotella intermedia) were more prevalent in tumor tissues.
statements.note: Lower diversity in tumour tissue and greater prevalence of these anaerobes and periodontopathogens are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumour mutation burden increased with the alpha diversity of intratumoral bacteria in the OSCC patients studied.
statements.evidence: The integrated analysis of the 5R 16S rRNA-seq and WES data revealed that tumor mutation burden was positively correlated with the α diversity of the intratumoral bacteria in OSCC patients.
statements.note: The integrated sequencing analysis reports a positive correlation between tumour mutation burden and intratumoral bacterial alpha diversity.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Intratumoral bacterial composition differed between smokers and non-smokers in this OSCC cohort.
statements.evidence: We found significant differences in bacterial profiles between tumors and adjacent normal tissues.
statements.note: Bacterial profiles are compared between tumour and adjacent normal tissue only; no patient subgroup such as smoking status is examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patients whose tumour tissue contained Dialister pneumosintes had poorer short-term disease-free survival.
statements.evidence: And the presence of Dialister pneumosintes within tumor tissues is associated with poorer short-term disease-free survival in OSCC patients.
statements.note: The abstract reports this association between intratumoral Dialister pneumosintes and short-term disease-free survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Screening 387 sequenced C. neoformans isolates found RNAi loss-of-function mutations in 7 of them, roughly 1.8%.
statements.evidence: Our results suggest that RNAi loss is relatively common (7/387, ~1.8%)
statements.note: The abstract gives the frequency of RNAi loss in the sequenced collection as 7 of 387 isolates, about 1.8%.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The RNAi-loss isolates that are not hypermutators grow more slowly than isolates with intact RNAi.
statements.evidence: Remarkably, several RNAi-loss isolates were identified that are not hypermutators and have not accumulated transposons.
statements.note: These isolates are described by their mutation rate and transposon content; no growth or fitness measurement is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Moving the RNAi loss-of-function mutations into a non-hypermutator strain that already carried a high transposon burden produced a hypermutator phenotype.
statements.evidence: To test whether these RNAi LOF mutations can cause hypermutation, the mutations were introduced into a nonhypermutator strain with a high transposon burden, which resulted in a hypermutator phenotype.
statements.note: The engineered strain is reported to have become a hypermutator, which is how the mutations were shown to be causal.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Crossing an RNAi-loss isolate with one carrying a high Cnl1 burden produced F1 hypermutator progeny that had inherited the large transposon load.
statements.evidence: when an RNAi-loss isolate was crossed with an isolate containing a high Cnl1 burden, F1 hypermutator progeny inheriting a high transposon burden were identified
statements.note: The cross is reported to have yielded hypermutator F1 progeny carrying the inherited high transposon burden.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The signature predicted survival in two separate patient sets, a TCGA cohort of 177 and a Rome cohort of 78.
statements.evidence: This model predicts survival outcomes in two independent cohorts of HCC patients (TCGA cohort, N = 177; Rome cohort, N78)
statements.note: Both cohort sizes are given with the statement that the model predicts survival outcomes in each.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The transcriptional signature also predicts which HCC patients respond to sorafenib.
statements.evidence: Despite the wealth of genomics data, treatment and prognosis are still dependent on clinical and pathological factors.
statements.note: The signature is evaluated against survival and immunogenomic features only; no drug or treatment response is examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A Wnt/beta-catenin transcriptional signature marked pathway activity whether or not pathway-activating mutations were present in the tumour.
statements.evidence: We have identified a Wnt/β-catenin-related transcriptional signature denoting pathway activity regardless of the presence of pathway-related activating mutations.
statements.note: The signature is reported as denoting pathway activity independently of activating mutations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: HCCs without CTNNB1 mutation that nonetheless carry the mutation-associated transcriptional footprint had unfavourable survival and immune-excluded microenvironments.
statements.evidence: A non-genetic state recapitulating the transcriptional footprint associated with CTNNB1 mutation identifies wild-type HCCs characterized by unfavorable survival outcomes and immune-excluded tumor immune microenvironment.
statements.note: The abstract attributes both the poor survival and the immune-excluded microenvironment to these CTNNB1 wild-type tumours.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: HPV ctDNA was positive in 22 of 28 prediagnostic case samples, a sensitivity of 79%, and negative in all 28 controls.
statements.evidence: HPV ctDNA results were positive in 22 of 28 prediagnostic samples from HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma cases (sensitivity 79%) with a maximum lead time of 7.8 years. HPV ctDNA results were negative in all controls (0 of 28, 100% specificity).
statements.note: Both figures are reported directly: 22 of 28 cases positive at 79% sensitivity, and 0 of 28 controls positive.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within four years of diagnosis, the ctDNA assay was more accurate than HPV antibody detection over the same interval.
statements.evidence: Diagnostic accuracy was highest within 4 years of cancer diagnosis and was higher than HPV Ab detection within the same timeframe (P = .004).
statements.note: The abstract states ctDNA accuracy exceeded HPV antibody detection within four years of diagnosis, with a P value.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The assay detects HPV ctDNA before diagnosis in patients with cervical cancer as well.
statements.evidence: Plasma samples from the Mass General Brigham Biobank collected 1.3-10.8 years prior to diagnosis from HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma patients (n = 28) and age- and sex-matched controls (n = 28) were blinded
statements.note: The cohort consists only of oropharyngeal cancer cases and matched controls; no other HPV-associated cancer is tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A machine-learning model trained and tested on a separate 306-sample cohort lifted detection to 27 of 28 cases and stretched the maximum lead time to 10.3 years.
statements.evidence: Application of a machine-learning model trained and tested on an independent cohort of 306 cases and controls increased the sensitivity of detection to 27 of 28 cases (overall sensitivity 96%) and the maximum lead time to 10.3 years.
statements.note: Both the rise to 27 of 28 cases and the longer 10.3-year lead time are reported for the machine-learning model.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Blocking METTL3 catalytic activity with STM2457 lowered global m6A and was enough on its own to drive human HMC3 microglia into a senescence-like inflammatory state.
statements.evidence: Here, we show that selective catalytic inhibition of METTL3 with STM2457 lowers global m6A and is sufficient to induce a senescence-like inflammatory state in human HMC3 microglia.
statements.note: The abstract reports catalytic inhibition as sufficient to induce the senescence-like state in these cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rather than broadly derepressing transposable elements, m6A inhibition drove cytoplasmic double-stranded RNA accumulation and a selective HERVK-associated response.
statements.evidence: Rather than causing broad transposable-element derepression, m6A inhibition promoted cytoplasmic double-stranded RNA accumulation and a selective HERVK-associated response.
statements.note: The reported result contrasts the absence of broad TE derepression with cytoplasmic dsRNA build-up and a selective HERVK response.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: STM2457 produces the same senescence-like inflammatory state in primary human microglia from aged donors.
statements.evidence: Together, our study identifies m6A as a safeguard against microglial senescence and suggests that reduced m6A-dependent RNA regulation may contribute to chronic inflammatory remodeling in the aging brain.
statements.note: The closing claim concerns the aging brain in general, but the experiments use the HMC3 cell line and no primary or aged-donor microglia.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The induced state featured more senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity, elongated morphology, reduced proliferation, Lamin B1 loss and remodelled nuclear architecture.
statements.evidence: This state includes increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, elongated cellular morphology, reduced proliferation, Lamin B1 loss, and remodeling of nuclear architecture.
statements.note: All five features are listed in the abstract as components of the senescence-like state.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Activating histone modifications were lost rapidly from duplicate genes and then built back up in enrichment as the paralogs grew older.
statements.evidence: We found that activating histone modifications are quickly lost in duplicate genes before gradually increasing in enrichment as paralogs age.
statements.note: This loss-then-recovery trajectory with paralog age is the reported finding for activating marks.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In D. discoideum, duplicate genes enriched for H3K9me3 are expressed at lower levels than their parent copies.
statements.evidence: Previous research in vertebrates has demonstrated a potential role for epigenetic factors in allowing triplosensitive genes to increase in copy number by regulating their expression post-duplication.
statements.note: Expression regulation is cited as earlier vertebrate work; this study measures histone modification enrichment and transposon proximity, not expression levels.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The repressive mark H3K9me3 was most enriched on the youngest paralogs, with heterochromatin spreading from transposable elements the likely cause.
statements.evidence: For the repressive modification H3K9me3, we found it was enriched in the youngest paralogs, and that this enrichment was likely mediated by heterochromatin spread from transposable elements.
statements.note: Enrichment in the youngest paralogs and transposon-derived heterochromatin spread as its likely mediator are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In human paralogs, H3K9me3 enrichment showed no significant link with triplosensitivity, whereas triplosensitivity was significantly associated with transposon proximity.
statements.evidence: while we found no significant link between enrichment for the repressive mark H3K9me3 and triplosensitivity in human paralogs, we did find a significant association between triplosensitivity and transposon proximity
statements.note: The abstract reports the null result for H3K9me3 and the significant association for transposon proximity side by side.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CDK1 was significantly higher in glioma tissue than in normal controls, and its expression climbed further with increasing tumour grade.
statements.evidence: The results indicated that CDK1 was significantly upregulated in glioma tissues compared with normal controls, with expression levels escalating with tumor grade.
statements.note: Both the upregulation versus normal tissue and the rise with tumour grade are reported results.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A pharmacological CDK1 inhibitor shrinks glioma tumours in mice.
statements.evidence: The robust association between CDK1 expression, tumor grade and survival, coupled with functional validation across complementary assays, positions CDK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy.
statements.note: CDK1 inhibition is proposed as a strategy on the basis of siRNA knockdown in cell lines; no drug treatment or animal experiment is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Silencing CDK1 reduced glioma cell proliferation, migration and invasion while increasing apoptosis and radiosensitivity.
statements.evidence: CDK1 knockdown attenuated glioma cell proliferation, migration and invasion, while enhancing apoptosis and radiosensitivity.
statements.note: The knockdown experiments are reported to move all five readouts in exactly these directions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patients with high CDK1 expression had shorter overall survival, and CDK1 held up as an independent prognostic marker.
statements.evidence: High CDK1 expression correlated with a reduced overall survival and served as an independent prognostic marker.
statements.note: The survival analysis reports reduced overall survival with high CDK1 and independent prognostic value.
